concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, along with the elevated prothrombin time and INR, suggest prosthetic valve thrombosis.

contradict_spans: blood and urine cultures were sterile
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of fever, bilateral knee pain, and elevated inflammatory markers suggest infective endocarditis, although the sterile blood and urine cultures argue against it.
The patient's anemia and elevated inflammatory markers suggest anemia of chronic disease.

support_spans: 4 days of progressive dyspnea on exertion
concepts.why: The patient's history of rheumatic mitral stenosis and symptoms of heart failure suggest rheumatic heart disease.
The patient's elevated prothrombin time and INR suggest a hemorrhagic diathesis.

rationales.F01: Dyspnea on exertion is a common symptom of prosthetic valve thrombosis.
rationales.F02: Orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea are also common symptoms of prosthetic valve thrombosis.
rationales.F08: Anemia can be a sign of anemia of chronic disease.
rationales.F10: Prolonged prothrombin time and elevated INR are indicative of prosthetic valve thrombosis and hemorrhagic diathesis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of low hemoglobin and elevated C-reactive protein, without other clear explanations, decided it.
